quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return to your lane.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle, you have enough space to return to your lane.

questions.question: After a train passes a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Even after a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not proceed until all gates are lifted and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
An intersection is coming.
Railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to something ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare for traffic or get ready to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
A divided highway is starting.
The lane ends.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: If water on the road causes your vehicle to lose traction, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to improve traction.
Brake hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, tires can lose contact with the road and ride on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into any traffic, wait for a large gap. This gap must be big enough for your vehicle to reach the same speed as the other traffic.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, do not cross until you can see clearly in both directions and no trains are coming.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual situations:

options.text: Causes traffic jams.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events. This habit, called rubbernecking, causes traffic jams.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink reduces your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful when turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars on the pavement mixes with rain, making the road slippery.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous when driving in a work zone?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic conditions and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch closely for workers and equipment.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: Windshield wipers cannot clear rain from the windshield.
Tires lose contact with the road.
Spray from a truck reduces visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. The car loses grip. This can happen at high speeds with water on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. Then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If weather or light conditions require headlights, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Where are truck blind spots located?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left of the cab.
On the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots behind and to the left. The driver cannot see a car in these areas. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss because they can hide in blind spots. Always look carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to see hazards around you. Do not stare only at the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: When passing, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
After you pass the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are far enough from the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
Press the brake pedal down hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Release the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow by itself. Use gentle braking only if needed. When safe, pull off the road.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting between lanes, and turning up the radio. When you notice these signs, park safely and take a short nap to refresh yourself.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers at construction sites. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.
